entries.claim: For the static stop-button phase, retain 90 controls as a low-confidence full-phase duration estimate, but recommend an initial 60-control visual progress review with an explicit stationary guard. A 90-control authorization WITH that guard reached its budget without a guard wake while a shallow noncontact down/up motion ended in above-button hovering. Once above-button hover, unproductive bobbing, or a recovery is visible, review a fresh VLA prefix within 16 controls rather than renewing a full-phase budget. Stationary monitoring remains useful for sustained lack of motion but cannot replace visual contact-progress review when movement interrupts its 32-control window. Neither this shorter interval nor one eventual success proves safety or intervention necessity.
